title: Hybrid queueing with SLO-aware slow-start and tenant hibernation
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: Dedicated GPU fleets see a mix of steady tenants and bursty newcomers. When new tenants suddenly ramp traffic they either overwhelm local KV caches and worker pools (leading to high tail latency) or we conservatively throttle them and violate their throughput expectations. Current admission controls are global-rate-first: they do not differentiate warm vs cold requests, and autoscaler reacts too late to prevent SLO violations.

This ticket implements a hybrid queueing + slow-start admission strategy that cooperates with autoscaling and a 'tenant hibernation' reclaim mechanism. Goals: preserve per-tenant throughput guarantees for committed tenants, provide a low-latency ramp for new traffic without destabilizing the fleet, enable reclaiming unused reservation capacity, and provide a safe soft-shed path under overload.

Key behaviors to deliver:
- Per-tenant slow-start: allow a controlled ramp of permitted concurrency/throughput for newcomers or traffic spikes based on historical footprint and immediate resource feedback.
- SLO-aware routing decisions: route requests to warm workers when possible; prefer warm routes for latency-sensitive classes. Fall back to cold routes only under defined conditions.
- Tenant hibernation: detect long-running idle reservations and automatically transition them to hibernation with quick reactivation paths; this frees reserved capacity for bursts while preserving reservation semantics.
- Soft-shed and fallback: when fleet is overloaded, prefer demotion to best-effort lane and graceful shedding based on estimated impact instead of outright drops.

This design must integrate with existing autoscaler hooks (scale-up signals) and dashboards for observability.
acceptance_criteria:
1) New hybrid admission policy can be toggled per-fleet and per-tenant config.
2) Slow-start ramps from baseline to target throughput within configurable time window (default 30s) and respects per-tenant reservation.
3) Warm-route preference reduces p99 tail by >=10% for latency-sensitive class in canary tests.
4) Tenant hibernation reclaims at least 20% of idle reserved capacity in test fixtures and can be reverted within 5s on traffic.
5) Soft-shed path drops are triaged to best-effort lane first; global drop rate under sustained overload is lower than current baseline.
6) End-to-end e2e load tests and regression suite created; metrics and dashboards validated in canary region.
design_notes:
Architecture summary:
- Ingress layer: small Decision Graph component evaluates per-request signals (tenant metadata, reservation status, current worker KV-warmth score, SLO class, recent error/latency telemetry).
- Admission controller: implements hybrid queue + token ramp. For new tokens we assign a slow-start budget that increments on successful responses and decrements on timeouts/errors.
- Routing: route selection prefers workers with KV-warmth >= threshold for SLO-sensitive requests. If no warm worker available, Decision Graph can either queue (if within latency budget) or route to cold path and mark telemetry.
- Hibernation controller: runs periodic scan of reservations with low recent ingress and issues hibernate operation (update reservation state, free GPU cache allocations). Re-activation uses a fast-path prewarm RPC to a minimal number of workers before accepting full traffic.

Algorithm sketches:
- SlowStartBudget(tenant): budget = max(min_reservation, historical_95th_rate * 0.25); every successful response -> budget += alpha; every error/timeout -> budget -= beta; enforced at admission gate.
- Warmness scoring: worker_warmness = weighted(KV_hit_ratio, recent_success_rate, recent_qps); prefer worker if warmness > 0.7.

Trade-offs considered:
- Aggressive hibernation risks cold-start penalties. Mitigation: fast prewarm during reactivation and conservative hibernation thresholds for SLO-sensitive tiers.
- Slow-start length vs throughput guarantees: expose configs per tenant and provide override for enterprise reserved contracts.

Interfaces and config:
- Fleet config entries: slow_start_window_s, slow_start_alpha, warmness_threshold, hibernate_idle_minutes, hibernate_grace_period_s.
- API flags for tenants: allow_hibernation (bool), slo_class (latency|throughput|best-effort), reservation_capacity.

test_plan:
Unit tests for Decision Graph rules, property tests for slow-start counters.
Integration tests in local cluster that emulate warm/cold workers.
Load tests:
- Scenario A: 100 tenants with reserved capacity; introduce 10 burst tenants and measure p50/p95/p99 and tail error rates.
- Scenario B: Rapid on/off traffic to test hibernation churn and reactivation latency.
- Scenario C: Sustained overload to validate soft-shed path and demotion logic.

Metrics to assert in tests: p99 latency, successful_qps_per_tenant, fraction_of_reserved_capacity_reclaimed, reactivation_time_ms.

Automation:
- Add e2e pipeline job: ci/e2e/hybrid-admission (runs synthetic workload and publishes to dashboard).
- Threshold gating: p99 regression must be < +5% on baseline for canary.
monitoring_and_rollout:
Dashboards:
- Canaries: 'hybrid-admission/canary/latency' (p50/p95/p99), 'hybrid-admission/canary/errors', 'hybrid-admission/hibernate/reclaimed_capacity'
- Telemetry emitted: tenant_id, reservation_id, budget_level, worker_warmness, admission_decision, reactivation_latency, shed_decision

Canary rollout plan:
- Stage 1: Enable feature flag on 5% of requests in canary region for best-effort tenants only. Observe 24h.
- Stage 2: Expand to 25% including throughput SLO tenants with overridden slow-start params. Observe 48h.
- Stage 3: 100% for canary region; run 72h soak and verify runbook steps.

Fallback steps:
- Feature flag off (fast path). If immediate degradation: revert admission gate (traffic continues under previous admission controller) and trigger incident runbook.

- Runbook: https://runbooks.redwood.ai/hybrid-admission
- Pager: SRE on-call -> escalation policy in runbook.
risks_and_mitigation:
Risk: Hibernation causes customer performance regressions on immediate reactivation. Mitigation: conservative defaults and allow tenant opt-out; fast prewarm RPC to 2 workers to reduce cold penalty.
Risk: Slow-start too conservative for enterprise customers with reserved throughput. Mitigation: reservation-aware bypass where tenants with contractual reservations can opt for immediate capacity up to reservation.
Risk: Telemetry overhead and decision graph latency. Mitigation: micro-benchmark Decision Graph; cache last decision per-tenant for 1s.
Risk: Interaction with autoscaler causing thrashing. Mitigation: add autoscaler stabilization window and scale signals from Decision Graph rather than raw QPS.
